She is a goddess who sparked a revolution in adult video.
With Kuroki, I might create something humanity has never seen before.

Allow me to ask you a question in return instead.
Wait—you mean me?
Yes, you. I am asking your heart, not your mouth.
Besides, you are truly beautiful, and your voice is wonderful!
Tell me, what are your true feelings deep down?
He is only joking, so please don't take him seriously.
Would you care for some black tea?
Yes, thank you. Excuse me.

lines.trans: Goodbye.

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.text: あの方はわたくしのいわば創造主でございますから。
examples.trans: To me, he is what you might call my creator.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: cause; bring about; wake someone up
meanings.note: Godan transitive verb; 騒ぎを起こす means 'cause a commotion'.

examples.text: 次に騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すぞ。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion next time, I'll throw you out.

examples.text: 朝七時に起こしてください。
examples.trans: Please wake me up at 7 a.m.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。
黒木君とならまだ人類が見たことがないものを作れるかもしれない。
examples.trans: With Kuroki, I might create something humanity has never seen before.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

examples.text: 互いに同じ時代に生きていてよかったと思える作品が撮れます。
examples.trans: We can shoot films that make us glad we lived in the same era.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 時代が変わりましたね。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: More formal counterpart of じゃあ used in business and polite conversation.

examples.text: では逆に質問させていただきます。
examples.trans: Allow me to ask you a question in return instead.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Expresses sudden surprise, shock, or disbelief.

examples.text: えっ、もう帰るんですか。
examples.trans: Huh, are you going home already?

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
In the idiom 口を出す, means 'to meddle / butt in'.
Noun.

examples.text: 心を開いて話しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's open our hearts and talk.

examples.text: 温かい心に感謝します。
examples.trans: I'm grateful for your warm heart.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: I-adjective describing beauty.

examples.trans: Mama, you're looking beautiful today too.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Everyday word for books and bound publications.

examples.trans: I buy a book at the bookstore.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Conjunctive particle giving a reason, softer than から.

examples.text: 雨が降っているので、家にいます。
examples.trans: Since it's raining, I'm staying home.

examples.text: 時間がないので急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.trans: Would you care for some black tea?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
